options: A special kind of variable that can only exist inside a Foreach Loop
An expression assigned to a read/write property of a task, container, log provider, or connection manager, recalculated at run time instead of staying fixed
A parameter that has been marked Required
The name for any expression that returns a string data type
questions.explain: A property expression attaches directly to a property, so that property's value gets recalculated from the expression at run time rather than sitting fixed.

questions.q: Which dialog does the Property Expressions Editor open when you click the ellipsis in its Expression column?
options: The Parameterize dialog box
The Expression Builder
SQL Server Management Studio
The Variables window
questions.explain: Clicking the ellipsis next to an expression in the Property Expressions Editor opens the Expression Builder, where you can drag in variables and functions graphically.

questions.q: How do you reach the property expressions of a connection manager specifically?
options: Only through the dtexec command-line utility
Select the connection manager in the Connection Managers area, then use the Properties window — connection managers don't have an Expressions page
Right-click the Data Flow task and choose Expressions
Through the Variables window's Grid Options
questions.explain: Connection managers are a special case: their property expressions can only be accessed through the Properties window after selecting the connection manager, not through an Expressions page like tasks and containers have.

questions.q: In the classic 'loop over files in a folder' pattern, what actually causes a Flat File connection manager to point at a different file on each iteration?
options: The package must be restarted between each file
SSIS automatically re-scans the folder without any configuration
A property expression on ConnectionString references the variable the Foreach Loop container updates on each pass
The Data Flow task itself is rebuilt on every iteration
questions.explain: The Foreach Loop container updates a variable with each file's path, and a property expression on the connection manager's ConnectionString — referencing that same variable — picks up the new value on every iteration.

questions.q: Relative to package configurations, when are property expressions evaluated?
options: Only if the package is run in debug mode inside SSDT
Before configurations load
After configurations load, but before validation and execution
At the exact same instant as configurations, with no defined order
questions.explain: Configurations load first and can update the variables a property expression depends on; the property expressions then evaluate using those updated values, before validation and execution.
